history.summary: The Surya Mandir at Surajpur (Baragaon) stands beside the sacred Suraj Pokhar (Sun Pond) and is counted among the 12 Suryadhams of India. The site has been a centre of sun worship for over a thousand years: Pala-era images of Surya, Vishnu, Shiva, Ganesha, Tara and Buddha have been unearthed around it, and the temple houses a striking five-foot idol of Goddess Parvati alongside other Hindu and Buddhist deities. Local tradition says the original pond-side shrine was shifted into the village in the 17th century to protect it from Mughal destruction. Mythology links the site to Samba (son of Krishna), who is said to have cured his leprosy by worshipping Surya here; bathing in the pond is still believed to cure skin diseases. name: Surya Mandir, Surajpur Baragaon
town_description: Baragaon, also called Surajpur, is a village about 1 km from the ruins of Nalanda University in Nalanda district, Bihar. It is one of Bihar's oldest centres of sun worship, grouped around the sacred Suraj Pokhar (Sun Pond) and the centuries-old Surya shrine. Pala-period sculptures recovered around the village testify to more than a thousand years of continuous worship. The village draws large crowds twice a year for Chhath Puja, the festival of sun worship.
